environment.scope: CPU/shared unpinned host; no exclusive reservation, GPU inference or training in these measurements.

changes.behavior: Snapshot buffered-byte and completion counts before committing a successful future. If a caller exception interrupts those updates or handle removal, restore this record and counters so append/close retries cannot double-account it. Previously committed records stay committed. Does not resubmit NPZ writes.

Use a private row-clear operation for internally generated unique, in-range changed-row indices and skip the empty-row call. Public reset retains type/dimension/uniqueness/range validation. Repeated identity benchmark flag and timed policy-call counts expose actual replanning frequency; ownership and tracking behavior remain covered by the integer queue oracle.

Build one boolean validity mask and multiply directly into float32 depth, avoiding float64 intermediate depth and a duplicate validity comparison. All output channels own independent arrays. Prototype source exactly matches the adopted complete render.py file.

initial_negative_control.trigger: One caller interruption immediately before successful future handle removal; two real completed episodes counted as three

real_collection_signals.scope: Real SIGINT/SIGTERM sent only to the isolated worker itself by a one-shot line tracer immediately before deleting a successfully accounted future. SIGTERM handler raises SystemExit143; no guarantee under default-killing SIGTERM or arbitrary bytecode cancellation. Real NPZ writes, manifest count/read-back, native writer thread exit and FD recovery checked; prior-round baseline deterministically counts its single episode twice.

large_executor_oracles.scope: Six integer dtype variants with 8192 environments against baseline and independent Python integer queues; per-row exact actions and policy-call counts on every control, repeated/skipped/wrapped metadata, extreme IDs, partial explicit resets, strided IDs and caller-owned output mutation. collection_fault_cycles.scope: 60 cycles of all 52 collection-interruption regression configurations with real background writes/NPZ readback. Tracked subclass preserves inherited collection bytecode; GC/weakrefs verify recorder release after each case, FD/Python threads return to baseline. Sampled RSS and small point-state payloads do not establish a hard memory limit or an arbitrary-bytecode interruption guarantee.

mixed_collection_faults.scope: Real successful and failed background writers in the same recorder, interrupted successful-handle removal after earlier storage failures, optional original with-body failure. Exact manifest/readback counts, failed identities, first exception/failure state and secondary close error checked; all recorder weakrefs released after GC and per-case FD/Python-thread baseline restored. Small point-state payloads; no arbitrary-bytecode or RSS bound guarantee.

executor.scope: Precomputed policy chunks, CPU act plus identity increment/repeat logic; one warmup and nine measured alternating pairs, no stress probes active; shared host, no pinning, no neural inference/physics. sparse_executor.scope: Supplemental sparse repeated-step identities; CPU act, observation increments/selected repeats and precomputed chunk gathering plus callback/row counters. One warmup plus nine alternating measured pairs; recording/executor stress active on shared host. Final action hash and policy/row counts match. Excludes physics/neural inference; no general training speed claim.

executor_call_profile.scope: cProfile actual measure including 32 warmup, 1000 timed and two allocation calls; counts only, profiling timings are not benchmark results. Internal reset avoids public ID validation; external reset retains that validation.

limits: All measurements are CPU reference workloads on a shared unpinned host; neural inference, GPU training, real robots and web delivery are outside these timings.

Continuous-frame executor measurements are essentially flat. Larger benefits occur with repeated observations and depend on affected-row count, frequency, N and action layout; no uniform executor or training throughput gain is established.

Raster depth-only and RGB/depth cases improve, but four-channel cases and the RGB-only control vary. Traced allocation peaks can remain flat when other channels dominate; they are not process RSS or GPU memory.

Whole-package acquisition timings include positive and negative cases. A uniform end-to-end acquisition gain has not been established; all paired samples and the earlier renderer-stage diagnostic are archived.

Fault tests cover single interruptions of successful collection bookkeeping, selected rollback/removal failures and shutdown waits; they do not establish transactional cancellation at every arbitrary bytecode or interruption during rollback itself.
SIGTERM controllers install a handler raising SystemExit143. Default process-killing SIGTERM cleanup is not claimed.

FD/Python-thread checks and recorder weakref collection apply to tested cases; sampled RSS and payload-size budgets are not general leak proofs or hard process-memory bounds. Optional test skips remain in the recorded environment.

final_process_audit.scope: Exact-run Python command-path scan; excludes reporter and unrelated jobs. Recording controller waits/reaps both worker processes.

evidence_archive.scope: Exact initial package source, final changed source/tests/benchmark excerpts, all harnesses, raw timings/profiles/logs and intentional prior-stage evidence. Synthetic datasets regenerate from scripts; optional external SDK assets and installed dependencies are excluded.
